summary:
Allwork.Space reports on survey research from Talker Research, commissioned by seafood brand Wild Planet, polling 2,000 US hybrid workers about lunch breaks and time outdoors during in-office workdays.

Key findings: 56% of respondents stay indoors all day beyond their morning and evening commute, and 85% sometimes skip their lunch break entirely. Despite that, 91% say taking a lunch break is essential, 63% think more highly of colleagues who take a real lunch break, and 78% would prefer to eat outdoors most workdays.

The research claims mental and emotional benefits from outdoor eating. Only 51% rate their happiness 4 or 5 out of 5 before lunch, rising to 66% after eating lunch outdoors. Workers eat lunch at their desk roughly 2.5 days per week while working, plus another 2.6 days per week eating at the desk while not working.

Motivations for going outside include the belief that fresh air resets focus (64%) and that screen breaks aid mental clarity (58%). Barriers are structural and cultural: too many meetings or tasks (29%) and constant pressure to stay available to colleagues (25%).

Even during breaks, unplugging is difficult. Respondents spend 61% of their lunch break on a device. Activities include scrolling social media (41%), responding to nonwork messages (37%), reading them (35%), and life admin like bill paying or scheduling appointments (31%). Work bleeds in too: 32% read work email, 28% respond, and 25% leave their work computer active.

Outside work, 67% say they are prioritizing outdoor time more than a few years ago, via walking (67%), time with family and friends (49%), and pet care (38%).

Sue Thanavaro, Brand Marketing Director at Wild Planet, frames outdoor meals as a low-effort mental and physical reset that encourages slowing down and disconnecting from screens.
